say: Can empty space make something from nothing?

Empty space is never perfectly still. Quantum physics says its energy is always jittering.
That jitter lets a particle and its antiparticle borrow a little energy and pop into existence, [0.25] just for an instant. Then they meet, and vanish.
But at the edge of a black hole, one of them can fall in, [0.2] while the other escapes.
And that escaping glow is real. It's called Hawking radiation, predicted in nineteen seventy-four, though nobody has detected it yet.
So who pays back the borrowed energy? [0.4] The black hole does, with its own mass.
A black hole as heavy as the Sun would need ten to the sixty-seven years to evaporate. [0.3] The universe is only thirteen point eight billion years old.
So even at the edge of a black hole, nothing is ever truly free.
